## Purpose and Entry Points
CLIProxyAPI is a Go-based local or deployable AI gateway. It exposes OpenAI/Responses, Gemini/Interactions, Claude, Codex, and Grok-compatible APIs, then routes requests to OAuth-backed CLI accounts, provider API keys, or compatible upstreams. The standalone server starts at `cmd/server/main.go`; auxiliary model-catalog fetch/validation commands are under `cmd/fetch_codex_models/main.go` and `cmd/fetch_antigravity_models/main.go`. The reusable embedding surface is the `sdk/` tree.

## Server and Protocol Edge
The HTTP server owns listener setup, route registration, middleware, management-server integration, reload behavior, and protocol multiplexing. It accepts normal HTTP, streaming responses, WebSocket paths, and a Redis queue protocol boundary. Core paths: `internal/api/server.go`, `internal/api/server_routes.go`, `internal/api/protocol_multiplexer.go`. Request logging and response wrapping occur before provider handling, while API-specific SDK handlers separate OpenAI, Gemini, and Claude wire contracts: `sdk/api/handlers/openai/openai_handlers.go`, `sdk/api/handlers/gemini/gemini_handlers.go`, `sdk/api/handlers/claude/code_handlers.go`.

## Request Execution Pipeline
Handlers normalize request context and metadata, resolve the requested model/provider, run interceptors, select an account/executor, and stream or return the translated result. The central execution boundary is between protocol handlers and the proxy service/conductor: `sdk/api/handlers/handlers_execution.go`, `sdk/cliproxy/service.go`, `sdk/cliproxy/auth/conductor.go`. The conductor implements multi-account selection, weighting, retries, cooldowns, quota/error handling, session affinity, and failover; it should be treated as the routing policy core rather than duplicated in individual executors.

## Translation and Compatibility Layer
Translation is a matrix from incoming API format to a target provider format and back, preserving tools, multimodal content, reasoning/thinking, signatures, and streaming semantics. Registry/pipeline abstractions live in `sdk/translator/registry.go`, `sdk/translator/pipeline.go`, and `internal/translator/translator/translator.go`. Provider-format implementations are isolated by source/target, e.g. `internal/translator/openai/claude/openai_claude_request.go`, `internal/translator/codex/openai/responses/codex_openai-responses_response.go`, and `internal/translator/gemini/openai/chat-completions/gemini_openai_request.go`. This is the main protocol-compatibility boundary; executors should receive provider-native payloads.

## Provider Executors and Authentication
Executors make upstream calls and implement provider-specific request construction, authentication refresh, response decoding, streaming, WebSocket lifecycle, and replay/signature behavior. Major implementations include `internal/runtime/executor/claude_executor.go`, `internal/runtime/executor/codex_executor.go`, and `internal/runtime/executor/antigravity_executor.go`, with Gemini, Kimi, xAI, AI Studio, Vertex, and OpenAI-compatible variants nearby. OAuth/token implementations are segregated from execution in `internal/auth/claude/oauth_server.go`, `internal/auth/codex/openai_auth.go`, and `internal/auth/xai/xai.go`. Upstream services include OpenAI/Codex, Anthropic/Claude, Google Gemini/Antigravity/Vertex/AI Studio, xAI Grok, and Kimi.

## State, Models, and Live Reconfiguration
Configuration defines providers, credentials, aliases, compatibility, retries, weights, concurrency, and plugin settings; it is loaded and normalized through `internal/config/config_load.go`, `internal/config/config_normalization.go`, and `config.example.yaml`. The model registry merges packaged definitions and updates them at runtime: `internal/registry/model_registry.go`, `internal/registry/models/models.json`. A watcher detects config/auth/model changes and dispatches reload effects without requiring process restart: `internal/watcher/watcher.go`, `internal/watcher/config_reload.go`. Credential/account state is managed by the SDK auth conductor and can use filesystem, Git/object, PostgreSQL cooldown, or Redis-backed infrastructure: `sdk/cliproxy/auth/store.go`, `internal/store/postgresstore.go`, `internal/redisqueue/queue.go`.

## Extensibility, Operations, and Runtime
A plugin host permits native plugins to provide auth, model routing, translators, lifecycle interceptors, executors, schedulers, and management extensions. Its ABI/RPC/loading boundary is in `internal/pluginhost/abi.go`, `internal/pluginhost/host.go`, and `internal/pluginhost/rpc_client.go`; install/registry handling is in `internal/pluginstore/registry.go`. Management APIs handle configuration, auth files/OAuth, plugins, logs, quota, and usage-facing operations via `internal/api/handlers/management/handler.go`. Deployment is container-oriented through `Dockerfile`, `docker-compose.yml`, and cluster-specific `docker-compose.cluster.yml`; the primary runtime is a Go binary, with optional Redis and PostgreSQL services.
